title: Quantization-Aware Healing: A Compressed 4-Bit Model Outperforming Its Full-Precision Original
summary: The article introduces Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH), a novel method for recovering compressed and quantized large language models (LLMs). QAH enables a 4-bit quantized model (e.g., GPT-OSS 120B compressed to 60B parameters) to outperform its full-precision (bfloat16) counterpart on 7 out of 9 benchmarks, including long-context reasoning and mathematical problem-solving. Unlike traditional quantization-aware training (QAT) or distillation (QAD), QAH distills knowledge directly from the original full-precision model, avoiding the limitations of recovering from a degraded checkpoint. The approach is more stable, faster to train, and reduces memory/compute costs while improving accuracy.
key_points: Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) is a method to recover compressed and quantized LLMs, enabling 4-bit models to outperform their full-precision versions.
QAH addresses the limitations of traditional healing methods (QAT and QAD) by distilling knowledge directly from the original full-precision model, not a degraded checkpoint.

Applied to a GPT-OSS 120B model compressed to 60B parameters and quantized to MXFP4, QAH outperformed the bfloat16 version on 7 of 9 benchmarks, including long-context reasoning (+7.4) and math (+5.6).
QAH is more stable and efficient than QAT, reaching peak performance in ~100 steps (vs. 700 for QAT) and avoiding degradation during prolonged training.
The 4-bit QAH model reduces weight memory by ~4x and compute per token by ~2x compared to the full-precision version, making it cheaper and more efficient to deploy.
QAH reframes quantization as an opportunity to improve model accuracy rather than a trade-off for efficiency.
